definitions.explanation: Sweat caused by fear, nervousness, or a close call rather than heat or exertion.

examples.english: I broke into a cold sweat.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}のスピーチを{聞|き}いて{冷|ひ}や{汗|あせ}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: Listening to his speech made me break out in a cold sweat.

examples.japanese: {車|くるま}がすぐそばを{通|とお}り{過|す}ぎて、{冷|ひ}や{汗|あせ}が{止|と}まらなかった。
examples.english: A car passed right by me and I couldn't stop the cold sweat.

notes: Most commonly appears in the collocations {冷|ひ}や{汗|あせ}をかく (to break into a cold sweat) and {冷|ひ}や{汗|あせ}が{出|で}る (cold sweat comes out). Used when describing nervousness, fear, or relief after a dangerous moment. Unlike {汗|あせ} alone, {冷|ひ}や{汗|あせ} always implies a psychological cause rather than physical heat.
